sections.h2: Who to call about a Wayne County tax bill
sections.html:
All three desks are in Monticello. Through the year, the PVA values the parcel, the Sheriff gathers payments, and the County Clerk inherits any bill still open in spring.

The PVA sits at 55 N. Main Street, Suite 107, Monticello, KY 42633, phone 606-348-6621. Beyond the usual weekday hours of 8 to 4, the office is open the first and third Saturday of the month, 8 a.m. to noon. That is the easiest time for a working owner to ask about a value or an exemption. For a lost bill or a payment question, call the Sheriff's Office in Monticello.

Rates are set by elected bodies: the fiscal court, the school board, and the special districts. The PVA only values property.

sections.h2: Due dates, discount and late charges
sections.html:
The Sheriff accepts payment through April 15, as laid out in KRS 134.015. Pay everything by November 1 and you keep 2 percent. Wait past January 31 and you owe 10 percent extra.

  • Up to November 1: the 2 percent discount.
  • November 2 through December 31: the amount printed on your bill.
  • All of January: 5 percent more.
  • February 1 through April 15: a 10 percent surcharge.

Frankfort can swap in a calendar of 30-day blocks if its mailing runs late, so trust the dates on your own bill. If you are unsure whether a payment reached the Sheriff in time, ask for a receipt or confirmation before the deadline passes, and keep it with your closing papers. Taxes owed for the year of sale are a point for the sales contract, so ask your agent or attorney how the proration will be handled.

sections.h2: How does an owner contest a Wayne County value?
sections.html:
A conversation at the PVA's counter has to come first. State rules do not allow an appeal to be filed without it, and the staff must explain the valuation method and keep notes. Then the steps below apply.

Appeal steps for Wayne County property owners
StepWhen
Public inspection of the rollThirteen days, starting the first Monday in May
Talk with the PVAAnytime after notices go out, before filing
Written appeal at the County ClerkClose of business the day after inspection ends
Hearing before the local boardBegins 25 to 35 days after inspection; sessions last up to five days

The board wants proof it can see: insurance policies, construction cost, listings, and the physical features of land and buildings. If you own near Lake Cumberland, photograph docks, decks, and outbuildings as they stood on January 1. Missing the hearing after filing cuts off a further appeal.

The exemption subtracts $49,100 from what is taxed on a person's own residence in 2025 and 2026. Qualifying means turning 65, or being ruled totally disabled by a federal program or a pension system. The state levy for 2025 is 10.6 cents per $100, with local districts adding their own rates.

  • File the state's homestead and disability form at the Wayne County PVA.
  • Proof of age can be a passport, license, or birth certificate.
  • Disability payments must have been received through the whole assessment period.
  • Owners with a service-connected disability, or a permanent total ruling from Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems, skip the yearly renewal.

The exemption goes with the person, not the parcel. After you sell, tell the PVA so it comes off, and the next owner can apply for theirs.

sections.h2: Do unpaid Wayne County taxes block a sale?
sections.html:
Not by themselves, but they come out of your proceeds. Under KRS 134.420 a delinquency lien can sit on the parcel for as long as eleven years, and any buyer's title company will insist that it be cleared.

Once at the Clerk the amount grows by a penalty, a Sheriff's add-on, and monthly interest. Clerk and county attorney commissions, mailing costs, and a lien recording fee follow, and a bill can climb well past its original size within weeks.

Beyond that, an investor can buy the certificate at a sale and add charges. Paying the Sheriff before April 15 sidesteps the path, and the sales contract should spell out who covers this year's bill.

sections.h2: Steps for selling with a tax balance
sections.html:
To get ready, call the Sheriff for this year's total and the Clerk for any earlier year that was turned over as a certificate of delinquency. Write down the amounts and the date you were quoted. Next, give those figures to your closing agent. The payoff goes on the settlement statement, comes out of what you receive at the table, and the lien is released so the buyer gets clear title.

An inherited cabin, a rental, or a house needing repairs can go to a cash buyer as-is, with the tax settled the same day. A cash sale skips the lender's inspection and repair list, so an old tax balance is one fewer thing that can stall the deal.

sections.h2: A tax year in Wayne County, start to finish
sections.html:
The calendar helps a seller plan. Assessment notices arrive in spring, and the roll is open to the public starting the first Monday in May. That stretch is your chance to question a value. Rates get voted afterward, and the bill comes in the fall.

Pay by November 1 if you can, since that is the only date that earns a discount. The printed amount holds through December. After that the cost rises: 5 percent in January, then 10 percent from February 1 until April 15. A bill still unpaid after that lands with the Clerk, and the added costs described above begin.

If you plan to list in the spring, check the November and December payment before anything else. A paid bill is clean on the title search, which leaves a buyer's agent with fewer questions.

Wayne County lies on the Tennessee border, with Monticello as its only city and the seat. Lake Cumberland and the Daniel Boone National Forest reach into the county. Wayne County keeps Eastern time, though its west and south edges trace the Central time line, so a lender or attorney across that line may be an hour apart.

Population was 19,597 in 2025, up 0.2 percent from 2020. There are 10,206 housing units against 8,074 households, and 69.1 percent of homes have owners living in them. Median home value is $135,700. Owners with a mortgage spend a median $1,100 a month and those without spend $342, which makes a paid-off house inexpensive to carry. Rents have a median of $727 a month. The county voted wet on November 3, 2020.

faqs.q: What are the Wayne County PVA's hours?
faqs.a: At 55 N. Main Street, Suite 107 in Monticello, the PVA opens weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., plus the first and third Saturday of the month 8 a.m. to noon. The phone is 606-348-6621.

faqs.q: Is there a discount for paying Wayne County tax early?
faqs.a: Yes, 2 percent for paying the entire bill by November 1. The printed amount holds through December, then 5 percent and later 10 percent are added.

faqs.q: Must I talk to the Wayne County PVA before I can appeal?
faqs.a: Yes. You must confer with the PVA or a deputy first, and then file with the County Clerk by closing time on the day after inspection ends.

faqs.q: How big is the Wayne County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It deducts $49,100 for 2025 and 2026 from the value of the home you live in. Owners 65 or older, or totally disabled, file at the PVA.

faqs.q: Who gets my Wayne County tax bill after April 15?
faqs.a: The County Clerk takes it as a certificate of delinquency backed by a lien. Interest and commissions accumulate, and an investor can purchase it at a sale.
